polish303BattleOfBritainContext.warning: The 203 and 29 Polish pilots include personnel attached to British and Polish squadrons. 126 is one squadron's credited victories, not independent German losses; counts of 957/972 total WW2 claimed destruction elsewhere need different scope reconciliation.

warnings: One original Polish historical institute says 972 fighter aerial victory credits while RAF Museum states 957; keep both as source-specific unverified comparison (15 difference).
73,524 is termed combat MISSIONS in institutional text; clarify whether individual aircraft combat sorties versus unit missions before using as denominators or comparing with RAF sortie tables.
Polish units and Polish crews flying RAF units already appear in RAF national statistics; avoid addition to RAF total.
Victory credit figures represent claimed destruction and fractional/shared credit rules, not actual independently confirmed German losses.

official2006MilitaryNarrative.warning: Broad Czechoslovak service includes pilots/crews in other RAF units, and perhaps different global/date scope than the named squadrons below; >300 are credited wartime claims, not verified Luftwaffe losses.

units.eventWindowWarning: The narrative includes a June 15, 1945 fatal flying-accident case AFTER May 9, so its 31 all-war KIA/accident total cannot automatically be treated as pre-May9 deaths.

units.note: Bomber Command to Coastal Command in 1942. The 246 are killed OR missing, cannot be equated to deaths; 2 submarines sunk are credited and require independent naval cross-check. The unit later performed postwar repatriation flights through 1946, excluded from Atlas.

cautions: Published 17,472 sorties / 10,364 flying hours yields less than 36 minutes per sortie; this unusual ratio may reflect mislabelled counts or different denominators. Preserve, investigate original ORB/diary before comparison.
Independent Jan Rajlich-based secondary says 17,427 sorties, 45 less than RAF Museum and Czech MOD 17,472.
English museum text says 1 damaged enemy aircraft while Czech museum version and Czech Ministry of Defence publication say 16. Use original Czech count with divergence annotation.

units.warning: The source explicitly includes June 7 1945 escort of the British royal family to Guernsey, AFTER Atlas cutoff; 8,944 all-unit total may also include this postwar activity. 30 mixes killed/missing/captured; not 30 deaths.

68 Squadron was a BRITISH RAF unit with Czech B Flight only; 1,905 / 4,095 are Czech participation figures, not the whole RAF 68 Squadron combat sortie total. Unlike distinct national squadrons, national attribution is to individual flight.

czechoslovakRAFHosted.derivedUnitSortiesWarning: 40,488 is a raw sum of published lifetime unit/flight sortie figures across dissimilar intervals and host structures.
